summary: Central Maine/Norridgewock Airport is a small general aviation facility serving the central Maine region, located in the town of Norridgewock near the Kennebec River. The airport primarily supports recreational flying, flight training, and private aircraft operations, offering pilots a convenient base in the scenic interior of Maine. Its rural setting makes it a popular stop for those exploring the lakes, forests, and small communities of central New England.
faqs:
Q: What type of airport is Central Maine/Norridgewock Airport?
A: It is a small general aviation airport primarily serving private, recreational, and training flights with no scheduled commercial service.

Q: Are there commercial flights available at OWK?
A: No, the airport does not offer scheduled commercial passenger service. It caters mainly to general aviation activities.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport features runways, tie-down areas, and basic services for general aviation aircraft, though amenities are limited given its small size.

Q: Can pilots get fuel at Norridgewock Airport?
A: Pilots should contact the airport operator in advance to confirm fuel availability, as self-service options may vary.
transport_tips: The airport is located just outside the small town of Norridgewock, roughly 20 miles northwest of Waterville, so a personal vehicle is the most practical way to reach it. Rental cars are not available on-site, so arranging ground transport in nearby towns is recommended. Major highways such as US Route 2 and I-95 provide regional access for visitors driving in.
local_tip: Plan your visit around daylight hours — the surrounding rural roads and approach paths are easiest to navigate when visibility is good, and nearby Lake George and the Kennebec River offer scenic spots worth visiting if you have time before or after your flight.
